newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso claws back to 1,101 against dlr.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso claws back to 1,101 against dlr.

text.p: Colombia's peso clawed back four pesos to close at 1,101 pesos to the dollar amid heavy market speculation, interbank traders said Thursday.

"There was a lot of speculation early in the day then the peso rate rose and then dropped back a bit again. The market was waiting for a large dollar inflow which is probably why the peso rose," one Bogota trader said.
Trader said industry, particularly the oil sector, poured dollar export earnings into the market while some banks moved to shorten dollar positions.
They said the market was likely to remain quiet Friday because of the July 4 holiday in the United States but predicted the peso could fall slightly.
Traders reported 333 deals worth a total $173 million. The peso opened at 1,104 to the dollar, hit an intraday high of 1,099.9 and sank to an intraday low of 1,105.9.
